ms.report:
The "Outputs", “Acceptance Criteria" and "Evidence of Milestone Completion" for this Milestone are all structured as points 1. 2. and 3. which we’ll title “Course outline”, “Marlowe environments” and “Course promotion” respectively.
Regarding 1. “Course outline” we have planned the 18 sessions (at 1.5hrs each). This outline can be found below. at the Catalyst proposal updates document https://45b.io/marlowe-workshops-24 .
Most sessions will be exploratory having this outline as a guide, not an itinerary. The reason we prioritize live workshops is to provide bilateral communication with learners and tailor content to their level and needs. Also, we should highlight our experience with the pilot project “Cardano for non-techs” in gathering resources on-demand and, as demonstrated in its recordings, articulating contents as necessary to ensure learners are progressing and oriented.
Although we will surely cover all the outlined content, we will likely have to manage skewing time more towards the initial background knowledge content. Also, we’ve included two topics for “Cardano Governance” and “Cardano Funding” which we feel will help make our learners more aware of the human and “Network State” side of Cardano, as well as opportunities to get funded and build on Cardano.
Regarding 2. “Marlowe environments” (and 0. “Marlowe team”) we confirm we have greatly developed our relationship with the Marlowe team (who meanwhile was spun off IOG and is now maintained ). Nicolas Henin, Thomas Rybarczyk, Simon Thompson are the core team members that are supporting our project. As per their advice, we will be running Marlowe Playground that is available at https://playground.marlowe-lang.org/ . Our project does not aim to take contracts into production, so Playground is all we will need.

ms.promise:
(please have a look on the "Discussion" panel in the bottom-left of this page for context on the Milestones structure)
1. Run sessions for Cohort#1 learners:
- The sessions will go over different stages titled "Workshops for background knowledge leveling", "Introduction to Marlowe", "Deconstructing Marlowe use cases", "Building a use case together" and "Prototyping your own idea".
- Learners will be invited to record an initial 2-3min video talking about their background and expectations for the course and also to do a Final project presentation;
2. Course promotion and gathering interested attendees for Cohorts #2 and #3:
- Identify communities in Cardano and elsewhere to captivate for this training
- Development organizations developing Web2 financial/business solutions
- Communities teaching the development of smart contracts through other languages
- Financial and business organizations who can benefit of Marlowe
